books.section: Topic 4.9 The Development of an American Culture, B. European Romanticism and American Culture

stimulus.text: Washington Irving's "Rip Van Winkle" (1819) tells of a Dutch settler in the Catskill Mountains who drinks with strange men, falls asleep for twenty years, and wakes to find his village changed: the portrait of King George III has become one of George Washington, and his neighbors argue about the new republic. Irving first invented the fictional historian Diedrich Knickerbocker in 1809 to tell a whimsical history of old New Amsterdam.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.9 B: Irving's humorous short stories, "Rip Van Winkle" (1819) and "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" (1820), portrayed a fanciful version of America, and in an 1809 novel he invented the fictional historian Diedrich Knickerbocker. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: Irving's invention of Diedrich Knickerbocker best illustrates which of the following?

options.text: A historian who documented New Amsterdam from Dutch archives
options.misconception: Knickerbocker writes a history, so it is easy to take him for a real historian.

options.text: The failure of American writers to find readers
options.misconception: Early American writers struggled, so it is easy to read any invention as a sign of failure.

options.text: Irving's wish to write only for British audiences
options.misconception: Irving sold books in Britain, so it is easy to think Britain was his only audience.

options.text: An American writer inventing a humorous, homegrown voice

rationales.A: Knickerbocker was invented by Irving; the stimulus calls him fictional, and the history is whimsical, not archival.
rationales.B: The Knickerbocker book sold well and made Irving famous; it was a success, not a failure.
rationales.C: Irving wrote American stories for American readers first, and British readers enjoyed them too.
rationales.D: A made-up Dutch historian telling jokes about old New York is an American voice, invented on the spot.
rationales.general:
1. Check the stimulus label. Knickerbocker is 'fictional,' and his history is 'whimsical.'
2. Ask what inventing him achieved. Irving gave America a comic storyteller of its own, not borrowed from Europe.
Background from the books: Irving's stories set the stage for the more serious American writers who followed.
Remember: an invented narrator can be the most original thing in a book.
